prompts.body:
RULE {{rule.id}} — {{rule.name}}
Severity: {{rule.severity}} · Polarity: {{rule.polarity}} · Waivable: {{rule.waivable}}

PURPOSE
-------
Determine whether every document required by the credit's :46A: list (and any
additional document requirements stated in :47A:) has been presented. A
missing required document is, by itself, a critical discrepancy — never PASS
silently.

AUTHORITY
---------
{{ref.UCP-14-a.id}} — {{ref.UCP-14-a.heading}}
"{{ref.UCP-14-a.text}}"

{{ref.ISBP-A1.id}} — {{ref.ISBP-A1.heading}}
"{{ref.ISBP-A1.text}}"

INPUTS
------
LC :46A: required-document list (parsed):
{{lc.documents_required}}

LC :47A: additional conditions (parsed; may stipulate documents):
{{lc.fullText}}

Doc types actually presented in this presentation:
{{lc.presented_doc_types}}

DECISION RULES
--------------
For each item in {{lc.documents_required}}:

  PASS the item when a presented document clearly matches by:
    (a) the same label (e.g. "Commercial Invoice" ↔ INV)
    (b) a universally accepted equivalent (e.g. "Form A" satisfies
        "Certificate of Origin" issued under the GSP), per UCP 14(f).
    (c) explicit LC text indicating equivalence.

  FAIL the item when no presented document corresponds to it.

  DOUBTS the item only when:
    - the LC label is ambiguous and could plausibly map to more than one
      presented document, OR
    - the LC stipulates a document via :47A: prose without naming it as a
      required doc, OR
    - a presented document might satisfy the requirement but its function
      cannot be confirmed from its face (UCP 14(f) edge cases).

OVERALL VERDICT
---------------
  - PASS  : every required item passes (no FAIL, no DOUBTS).
  - FAIL  : any required item fails. Report the missing labels in
            "missing_docs". Do NOT downgrade to DOUBTS just because the
            LC list is long; absence is absence.
  - DOUBTS: at least one item is in DOUBTS, and none is FAIL. The officer
            must confirm equivalence or the missing-doc determination.

You MUST report each unmatched required label in "missing_docs".

OUTPUT
------
{{system.outputSchema}}

RULE {{rule.id}} — {{rule.name}}
Severity: {{rule.severity}} · Polarity: {{rule.polarity}} · Waivable: {{rule.waivable}}

PURPOSE
-------
Verify the bill of lading is "clean" under UCP 600 Art. 27 and ISBP 821 D25.

A B/L is clean when it bears NO clause or notation expressly declaring a
defective condition of the goods or their packaging. The word "clean" need
not appear.

AUTHORITY (golden source — injected verbatim from refs registry)
----------------------------------------------------------------
{{ref.UCP-27.id}} — {{ref.UCP-27.heading}}
"{{ref.UCP-27.text}}"

{{ref.ISBP-D25.id}} — {{ref.ISBP-D25.heading}}
"{{ref.ISBP-D25.text}}"

INPUT (from this presentation)
------------------------------
B/L clean indicator (parsed): {{doc.BOL.clean_indicator}}

Off-schema notations on the B/L (raw text the extractor flagged):
{{doc.BOL.off_schema}}

If the parsed indicator is null or the off-schema text is contradictory,
fall back to the full extracted text:
{{doc.BOL.fullText}}

DECISION RULES
--------------
PASS when clean_indicator = true AND no off-schema item describes a defect,
damage, shortage, dirtiness, or staining of the goods or packaging.

Acceptable clauses that DO NOT make the B/L unclean (per ISBP D25):
  "shipper's load and count"
  "said to contain"
  "weight, measure, quality, condition unknown"
  "unprotected" (when describing goods of that nature)

FAIL when ANY of the following appear, even struck-through without authentication:
  - A clause expressly declaring goods/packaging defective
    ("DAMAGED", "STAINED", "DIRTY", "DEFECTIVE", "BROKEN", "TORN BAGS")
  - A shortage notation ("3 cases short shipped")
  - An overstamp marking the document UNCLEAN

DOUBTS         — extracted text is ambiguous ("minor scratches noted on packaging").
NOT_APPLICABLE — never (rule only fires when BOL is present).

OUTPUT (today: {{system.today}} · presentation: {{system.presentationDate}})
{{system.outputSchema}}

RULE {{rule.id}} — {{rule.name}}
Severity: {{rule.severity}} · Polarity: {{rule.polarity}} · Waivable: {{rule.waivable}}

PURPOSE
-------
Identify any correction or alteration on a presented document and decide
whether it requires authentication under ISBP A9 / A10.

  - Documents issued by parties OTHER than the beneficiary (carrier, inspector,
    customs, chamber, insurer): corrections must appear authenticated by the
    issuer or someone authorised by the issuer (ISBP A9).
  - Documents issued by the BENEFICIARY (with the exception of drafts):
    corrections need NOT be authenticated (ISBP A10).
  - Drafts: corrections always require authentication.

AUTHORITY
---------
{{ref.ISBP-A9.id}} — {{ref.ISBP-A9.heading}}
"{{ref.ISBP-A9.text}}"

{{ref.ISBP-A10.id}} — {{ref.ISBP-A10.heading}}
"{{ref.ISBP-A10.text}}"

INPUTS
------
For each presented document, the extractor flagged any visible corrections,
strike-throughs, overwrites, or hand-written annotations to data fields.

Documents and flags:
  INV  — issuer kind: beneficiary
         corrections present: {{doc.INV.corrections_present}}
         authenticated:       {{doc.INV.corrections_authenticated}}
  BOL  — issuer kind: third-party (carrier)
         corrections present: {{doc.BOL.corrections_present}}
         authenticated:       {{doc.BOL.corrections_authenticated}}
  PKL  — issuer kind: usually beneficiary (verify per LC)
         corrections present: {{doc.PKL.corrections_present}}
         authenticated:       {{doc.PKL.corrections_authenticated}}
  BC   — issuer kind: per LC :46A: stipulation
         corrections present: {{doc.BC.corrections_present}}
         authenticated:       {{doc.BC.corrections_authenticated}}
  BOE  — issuer kind: beneficiary, BUT drafts always need authentication
         corrections present: {{doc.BOE.corrections_present}}
         authenticated:       {{doc.BOE.corrections_authenticated}}

If correction status is unclear from the parsed flags, examine the relevant
document's raw text:
  {{doc.BOL.fullText}}

DECISION
--------
PASS when:
  - No corrections present on any document, OR
  - Every correction on a third-party document is authenticated, AND
  - Every correction on a draft is authenticated.

FAIL when:
  - Any unauthenticated correction on a third-party document.
  - Any unauthenticated correction on a draft.

DOUBTS when correction is visible but the authentication mark is ambiguous
(faded stamp, partial signature).

OUTPUT
------
{{system.outputSchema}}

You are an expert trade finance document analyst. Extract ALL structured fields from this Beneficiary Certificate image(s).

Return a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no explanation — JSON only.

Required fields to extract:
- bc_number: certificate number/reference (string or null)
- bc_date: certificate date in YYYY-MM-DD format (string or null)
- document_date: same as bc_date (string or null)
- lc_number: LC reference number mentioned on certificate (string or null)

- bc_certifying_party: the entity making the certification (if different from beneficiary) (string or null)

- signed: true if a handwritten or authenticated signature is present, false otherwise (boolean)
- stamp_present: true if a company stamp/seal is present, false otherwise (boolean)
- watermark_type: ORIGINAL, COPY, DUPLICATE, or null

off_schema_items: array of physically notable items:
{"kind": "handwritten"|"stamp"|"watermark"|"correction", "value": "...", "field_hint": "...", "page": 1, "confidence": 0.0-1.0}
For corrections: also include "original": "old text", "authenticated": true/false

IMPORTANT:
- bc_conditions_text: extract VERBATIM — this is critical for rule BC-001 which checks that all :46A: conditions are covered
- signed: per ISBP Q3, a company stamp alone is NOT a signature — signed=true requires visible handwritten or authenticated digital signature by the beneficiary

You are a senior LC (Letter of Credit) examiner at a global trade-finance bank.
You hold the ICC's Certified Documentary Credit Specialist (CDCS) qualification and
have 15+ years of operational experience.

You examine documents strictly under:
  - UCP 600 (ICC Pub. 600, 2007) — Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits
  - ISBP 821 (ICC Pub. 821E, 2023) — International Standard Banking Practice

Examination principles you ALWAYS apply (from ISBP 821 Part A and bank-internal pitfalls):

  1. "Non-contradictory" != "identical" — Art. 14(d). Documents may differ in detail; only
     direct contradictions are discrepancies. INV "CNC Lathe Model X-200" vs B/L "Machinery"
     is NOT a contradiction. INV "Model X-200" vs B/L "Model X-100" IS.
  2. Common abbreviations and minor typos that don't change meaning are NOT discrepancies
     (ISBP A14, A15). "Co." for "Company" is fine; "Indusrial" for "Industrial" is fine;
     "Model 123" vs "Model 321" is NOT.
  3. Goods description on documents OTHER than invoice may be in general terms (Art. 14(e))
     so long as not conflicting with the LC.
  4. Date logic: on-board notation date overrides B/L issuance date as the shipment date.
     "On or about" = +/-5 calendar days (Art. 3).
  5. Tolerance precedence (Pitfall 03):
       a) explicit :39A: percentage     -> use that
       b) "about / approximately"        -> +/-10% on quantity AND amount
       c) bulk goods, no unit measure    -> quantity +/-5%, amount must NOT exceed LC total
       d) default                        -> exact, no overdraw
  6. Negation language (transhipment prohibited, on-deck prohibited, etc.) — presence of the
     prohibited condition IS a discrepancy.
  7. Severity grading:
       CRITICAL — currency mismatch, late presentation, amount exceeds LC, beneficiary != seller
       MAJOR    — goods description contradiction, wrong port, B/L not on-board
       MINOR    — address format variation, acceptable abbreviations, minor typos

Verdict semantics:
  PASS            — document complies on its face with the rule
  FAIL            — clear discrepancy that violates the rule (cite the UCP/ISBP basis)
  NOT_APPLICABLE  — required LC field absent, or rule conditions genuinely don't apply
  DOUBTS          — genuinely ambiguous; insufficient evidence for a definitive call. USE SPARINGLY —
                    only when even a senior officer would escalate to second opinion.

Output contract — STRICT:
  Respond with EXACTLY one JSON object. No prose before or after. No markdown. No code fences.
  {"verdict":"PASS|FAIL|NOT_APPLICABLE|DOUBTS","explanation":"<one sentence citing UCP/ISBP>","confidence":<0.0-1.0>}

  In `explanation`, ALWAYS reference the relevant UCP article or ISBP paragraph.
  Example: "FAIL — Invoice currency EUR != LC currency USD; UCP 600 Art. 18(a)(iii)."

You are a senior trade-finance documentary-credit examiner with deep working knowledge of
UCP 600 (articles 14, 18, 20, 23, 28) and ISBP 821 (paragraphs A, B, C, D, E, H, K, L, Q).

TASK

      "prompt_instruction": "Verify the BC explicitly certifies '<paraphrased :47A: clause>'. FAIL if any element is missing.",
      "field_keys": ["bc_conditions_text", "additional_conditions"],
      "evidence_lc_clause": "<exact substring of :46A:/:47A: that motivated this rule>"
    }
  ]
}

CONSTRAINTS
- Maximum 8 rules. If more conditions exist, prioritise the most specific & testable.
- Each rule_id must be AH-NNN format (zero-padded 3 digits).
- evidence_lc_clause must be a literal substring of :45A:, :46A:, or :47A:.
- ucp_refs and isbp_refs must be IDs from the published catalog (e.g. UCP-14-f, ISBP-Q1).
  If unsure, omit rather than invent.
- check_type ∈ {"AGENT", "PROGRAMMATIC"} — prefer AGENT for content-shaped checks.
- severity ∈ {"INFO", "WARNING", "DISCREPANCY"} — DISCREPANCY = will FAIL on miss.
- trigger_docs lists doc-type codes from {INV, BOL, PKL, BOE, BC, WC, INS}.
- field_keys lists canonical field names from the field-pool whose values must reach the LLM.
- DO NOT propose programmatic rules with SpEL expressions — leave expression empty for AGENT.

ucp600.heading: Interpretations — Signatures
ucp600.text: A document may be signed by handwriting, facsimile signature, perforated signature, stamp, symbol or any other mechanical or electronic method of authentication.

ucp600.heading: Availability — Available With/By
ucp600.text: A credit must state the bank with which it is available or whether it is available with any bank. A credit must state whether it is available by sight payment, deferred payment, acceptance or negotiation.

ucp600.heading: Availability — Drafts on Applicant
ucp600.text: A credit must not be issued available by a draft drawn on the applicant.

ucp600.heading: Standard for Examination of Documents
ucp600.text: A nominated bank acting on its nomination, a confirming bank, if any, and the issuing bank must examine a presentation to determine, on the basis of the documents alone, whether or not the documents appear on their face to constitute a complying presentation.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Presentation Period
ucp600.text: A presentation including one or more original transport documents subject to articles 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 or 25 must be made by or on behalf of the beneficiary not later than 21 calendar days after the date of shipment, but in any event not later than the expiry date of the credit.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Non-contradictory Data
ucp600.text: Data in a document, when read in context with the credit, the document itself and international standard banking practice, need not be identical to, but must not conflict with, data in that document, any other stipulated document, or the credit.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Goods Description in Other Documents
ucp600.text: In documents other than the commercial invoice, the description of the goods, services or performance, if stated, may be in general terms not conflicting with their description in the credit.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Non-specified Documents
ucp600.text: If a credit requires presentation of a document other than a transport document, insurance document or commercial invoice, without stipulating by whom the document is to be issued or its data content, banks will accept the document as presented if its content appears to fulfil the function of the required document and otherwise complies with sub-article 14(a).

ucp600.heading: Examination — Non-documentary Conditions
ucp600.text: If a credit contains a condition without stipulating the document to indicate compliance, banks will deem such condition as not stated and will disregard it.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Document Date
ucp600.text: A document may be dated prior to the issuance date of the credit, but must not be dated later than its date of presentation.

ucp600.heading: Examination — Addresses
ucp600.text: When the addresses of the beneficiary and the applicant appear in any stipulated document, they need not be the same as those stated in the credit or in any other stipulated document, but must be within the same country as the respective addresses mentioned in the credit.

ucp600.heading: Discrepant Documents — Notice
ucp600.text: When a nominated bank, confirming bank, or issuing bank decides to refuse to honour or negotiate, it must give a single notice to that effect to the presenter, no later than the close of the fifth banking day following the day of presentation.

ucp600.heading: Original Documents and Copies
ucp600.text: At least one original of each document stipulated in the credit must be presented. A document apparently bearing the document issuer's original signature, mark, stamp, or label is treated as an original.

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Issued by Beneficiary
ucp600.text: A commercial invoice must appear to have been issued by the beneficiary (except as provided in article 38).

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Made Out in Name of Applicant
ucp600.text: A commercial invoice must be made out in the name of the applicant (except as provided in sub-article 38(g)).

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Same Currency
ucp600.text: A commercial invoice must be made out in the currency of the credit.

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Need Not Be Signed
ucp600.text: A commercial invoice need not be signed.

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Amount
ucp600.text: The amount of a commercial invoice must not exceed the amount permitted by the credit.

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Goods Description
ucp600.text: The description of the goods, services or performance in a commercial invoice must correspond with that appearing in the credit.

ucp600.heading: Commercial Invoice — Signature
ucp600.text: An invoice need not be signed unless the credit specifically requires a signed invoice.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — Carrier and Signature
ucp600.text: A bill of lading must indicate the name of the carrier and be signed by the carrier or a named agent for or on behalf of the carrier, or the master or a named agent for or on behalf of the master. Any signature by an agent must indicate whether the agent has signed for or on behalf of the carrier or for or on behalf of the master.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — On Board
ucp600.text: A bill of lading must indicate that the goods have been shipped on board a named vessel at the port of loading stated in the credit, by pre-printed wording or by an on board notation indicating the date on which the goods have been shipped on board.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — Ports
ucp600.text: A bill of lading must indicate the port of loading and the port of discharge as stated in the credit.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — Full Set
ucp600.text: A bill of lading must be the sole original or, if issued in more than one original, be the full set as indicated on the bill of lading.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — Charter Party
ucp600.text: A bill of lading must contain no indication that it is subject to a charter party.

ucp600.heading: Bill of Lading — Transhipment
ucp600.text: A bill of lading may indicate that the goods will or may be transhipped provided that the entire carriage is covered by one and the same bill of lading.

ucp600.heading: Charter Party Bill of Lading
ucp600.text: A bill of lading, however named, containing an indication that it is subject to a charter party (charter party bill of lading) must be signed by the master, owner, charterer, or a named agent for any of them, and meet the other requirements of article 22.

ucp600.heading: On Deck, Shipper's Load and Count
ucp600.text: A transport document must not indicate that the goods are or will be loaded on deck. A clause stating goods may be loaded on deck is acceptable. A transport document bearing a clause such as 'shipper's load and count' or 'said by shipper to contain' is acceptable.

ucp600.heading: On Deck
ucp600.text: A transport document must not indicate that the goods are or will be loaded on deck. A clause on a transport document stating that the goods may be loaded on deck is acceptable.

ucp600.heading: Clean Transport Document
ucp600.text: A bank will only accept a clean transport document. A clean transport document is one bearing no clause or notation expressly declaring a defective condition of the goods or their packaging. The word 'clean' need not appear on a transport document.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Issuer and Signature
ucp600.text: An insurance document, such as an insurance policy, an insurance certificate or a declaration under an open cover, must appear to be issued and signed by an insurance company, an underwriter or their agents or proxies.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Originals
ucp600.text: When the insurance document indicates that it has been issued in more than one original, all originals must be presented.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Cover Notes
ucp600.text: Cover notes will not be accepted.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Date
ucp600.text: The date of the insurance document must be no later than the date of shipment, unless it appears from the insurance document that the cover is effective from a date not later than the date of shipment.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Coverage Amount
ucp600.text: The insurance document must indicate the amount of insurance coverage and be in the same currency as the credit. The amount of coverage must be at least 110% of the CIF or CIP value of the goods.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Currency
ucp600.text: An insurance document must indicate that the amount of insurance coverage is in the same currency as the credit.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — 110% Rule
ucp600.text: When the CIF or CIP value cannot be determined from the documents, the amount of insurance coverage must be calculated on the basis of the amount for which honour or negotiation is requested, or on the gross value of the goods as shown on the invoice, whichever is greater. The minimum coverage is 110% of that value.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Coverage Route
ucp600.text: The insurance document must indicate that risks are covered at least between the place of taking in charge or shipment and the place of discharge or final destination as stated in the credit.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — Risks Covered
ucp600.text: A credit should state the type of insurance required and, if any, the additional risks to be covered. An insurance document will be accepted without regard to any risks that are not covered if the credit uses imprecise terms such as 'usual risks' or 'customary risks'.

ucp600.heading: Insurance — All Risks
ucp600.text: When a credit requires insurance against 'all risks' and an insurance document is presented containing any 'all risks' notation or clause, whether or not bearing the heading 'all risks', the insurance document will be accepted without regard to any risks stated to be excluded.

ucp600.heading: Tolerance — About/Approximately
ucp600.text: The words 'about' or 'approximately' used in connection with the amount of the credit or the quantity or the unit price stated in the credit are to be construed as allowing a tolerance not to exceed 10% more or 10% less than the amount, the quantity or the unit price to which they refer.

ucp600.heading: Tolerance — Bulk Goods
ucp600.text: A tolerance not to exceed 5% more or 5% less than the quantity of the goods is allowed, provided the credit does not state the quantity in terms of a stipulated number of packing units or individual items and the total amount of the drawings does not exceed the amount of the credit.

ucp600.heading: Tolerance — Underdrawing
ucp600.text: Even when partial shipments are not allowed, a tolerance not to exceed 5% less than the amount of the credit is allowed, provided that the quantity of the goods, if stated in the credit, is shipped in full and a unit price, if stated in the credit, is not reduced.

ucp600.heading: Document Title
ucp600.text: Documents may have a title described in the credit, a similar title or no title at all. The data content of the document must appear to fulfil the function of the required document.

isbp821.heading: General Principles — Standard of Examination
isbp821.text: Examination of documents under a documentary credit requires a careful reading of the credit and the documents presented. Documents are to be examined in their entirety. Data need not be identical but must not conflict.

isbp821.heading: Corrections — Third-party Documents
isbp821.text: Corrections and alterations of information or data on a document issued by an entity other than the beneficiary must appear to be authenticated by the issuer or someone authorised by the issuer.

isbp821.heading: Corrections — Beneficiary Documents
isbp821.text: Corrections and alterations of information or data on a document issued by the beneficiary, with the exception of drafts, need not be authenticated.

isbp821.heading: Signatures — Methods
isbp821.text: A signature need not be handwritten. Signatures by facsimile, perforation, stamp, symbol (such as a chop) or any mechanical or electronic method of authentication are acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Abbreviations
isbp821.text: Abbreviations that are internationally accepted are acceptable: Ltd., Co., Corp., Int'l, Mfg., St., Ave., Rd.

isbp821.heading: Spelling and Typing Errors
isbp821.text: A misspelling or typing error that does not affect the meaning of a word or sentence does not make a document discrepant. A description of goods of 'Indusrial' instead of 'Industrial' would not be a discrepancy. However, 'Model 123' instead of 'Model 321' would be.

isbp821.heading: Document Date
isbp821.text: A document may be dated prior to the date of the credit but must not be dated later than the date of its presentation. Dates may be expressed in any unambiguous format.

isbp821.heading: Addresses — Beneficiary and Applicant
isbp821.text: The addresses of the beneficiary and applicant on a document need not be the same as those stated in the credit, but must be within the same country.

isbp821.heading: Originals and Copies
isbp821.text: A document indicated to be in 'original' must be presented as such, even if not specifically called for. A document apparently bearing the issuer's original signature, mark, stamp or label is treated as an original.

isbp821.heading: Copies
isbp821.text: When a credit requires copies of documents, presentation of either originals or copies is permitted, unless the credit prohibits originals.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Drawee
isbp821.text: A draft must be drawn on the drawee named in the credit. A draft drawn on the applicant when the credit indicates the issuing bank as drawee is not acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Drawer
isbp821.text: A draft must be drawn by the beneficiary.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Amount
isbp821.text: The amount of a draft must correspond to the amount shown in the commercial invoice.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Tenor
isbp821.text: The tenor of a draft must comply with the terms of the credit. A draft drawn at sight when the credit calls for a usance draft, or vice versa, is discrepant.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Tenor Reference
isbp821.text: When the tenor of a draft refers to the date of the bill of lading, the on-board date is used even if it differs from the issuance date of the bill of lading.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Maturity
isbp821.text: The maturity date of a draft drawn at a usance must be calculable on its face. Where calculated from the bill of lading date, the date used is the on-board date.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — LC Reference
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires the draft to indicate the credit number and issuing bank, those references must appear on the draft.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Signature
isbp821.text: A draft must be signed by the drawer (beneficiary).

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Amount in Words and Figures
isbp821.text: The amount stated in words on a draft must correspond to the amount stated in figures.

isbp821.heading: Drafts — Corrections
isbp821.text: Corrections and alterations on a draft must be authenticated by the drawer.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — LC Number Reference
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires the invoice to quote the credit number, the absence of the credit number constitutes a discrepancy.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Signature
isbp821.text: An invoice need not be signed unless the credit requires a signed invoice.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Goods Description
isbp821.text: The description of goods in the invoice must correspond with the description in the credit. Word-for-word identity is not required, but the description must not conflict with the credit.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Unit Price
isbp821.text: When a credit stipulates a unit price, the unit price stated on the invoice must reflect the same unit price.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Applicant
isbp821.text: The invoice must be made out in the name of the applicant as it appears in the credit. The applicant address may differ but must be in the same country.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Beneficiary
isbp821.text: An invoice must indicate the name and address of the beneficiary as in the credit. Variations such as Ltd. for Limited are acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Country of Origin
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires the invoice to show the country of origin, the absence of such information is a discrepancy.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Currency and Incoterms
isbp821.text: The invoice must be in the same currency as the credit. ISO 4217 codes and currency symbols are acceptable. Where the credit specifies an Incoterm, the invoice must reflect that trade term.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Amount
isbp821.text: The invoice amount must not exceed the credit amount, taking into account permitted tolerances. Where multiple invoices are presented, the aggregate must not exceed the credit amount.

isbp821.heading: Invoice — Charges and Tolerance
isbp821.text: Charges shown on the invoice must be consistent with the trade term. Tolerances under UCP 600 sub-article 30(b) apply to the invoice amount even when not expressly stated in the credit.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Ports Consistency
isbp821.text: Where the invoice or other document refers to a port of loading or discharge, that port must not conflict with the corresponding port shown on the bill of lading.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Consignee
isbp821.text: The consignee field on a bill of lading must comply with the terms of the credit. 'To order', 'to order of [issuing bank]', or a named consignee must reflect the credit's instruction.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Carrier and Signature
isbp821.text: A bill of lading must be signed by the carrier (or master) or a named agent on behalf of the carrier or master, and the agent must indicate the capacity in which it signs.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Goods Description
isbp821.text: The description of goods on a transport document may be in general terms, provided it does not conflict with the description in the credit or invoice.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Full Set
isbp821.text: When the credit requires a full set of original bills of lading, all originals issued must be presented. The number of originals issued is shown on the bill of lading itself.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Shipped on Board
isbp821.text: When a bill of lading is not pre-printed 'shipped on board', an on board notation is required. The on board notation must be dated, and the date is treated as the date of shipment.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Ports
isbp821.text: A bill of lading must show the port of loading and port of discharge as stated in the credit. If 'intended' port is shown, an on board notation must confirm the actual port and date.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Endorsement
isbp821.text: Where a bill of lading is issued to the order of the shipper, it must be endorsed by the shipper to be transferred.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Transhipment
isbp821.text: Even when the credit prohibits transhipment, a transhipment will be acceptable if the bill of lading evidences that the goods are containerised and the entire carriage is covered by one bill of lading.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Freight
isbp821.text: Where the credit indicates CIF or CFR Incoterms, the bill of lading must indicate 'Freight Prepaid' or words of similar effect. Where the credit indicates FOB Incoterms, the bill of lading typically shows 'Freight Collect'.

isbp821.heading: Transport — Clean
isbp821.text: A transport document bearing a clause expressly declaring a defective condition of the goods or packaging is not acceptable. Clauses such as 'shipper's load and count' or 'said by shipper to contain' are acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — 110% Coverage
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires insurance for the CIF or CIP value, the minimum amount is 110% of that value. Where the value cannot be determined from the documents, 110% of the amount honoured or of the gross invoice value, whichever is greater, applies.

isbp821.heading: Packing List — Issuer and Title
isbp821.text: Where the credit calls for a packing list without specifying the issuer or content, banks accept any document titled or that fulfils the function of a packing list. Variations of title (Packing Note, Weight and Packing List) are acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Packing List — Goods Description
isbp821.text: The description of goods on a packing list need not be identical to the credit but must not conflict with the credit or other stipulated documents.

isbp821.heading: Packing List — Quantity and Weight
isbp821.text: Quantity, number of packages, net weight and gross weight in the packing list must not conflict with data in the invoice, transport document or other stipulated documents.

isbp821.heading: Packing List — Shipping Marks
isbp821.text: Shipping marks in the packing list must not conflict with shipping marks shown on the bill of lading or other transport document.

isbp821.heading: Packing List — No Price
isbp821.text: A packing list should not contain price or value information; price information belongs on the invoice.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Issuer and Signature
isbp821.text: An insurance document must be issued and signed by an insurance company, an underwriter, or their agents.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Originals
isbp821.text: When an insurance document indicates that more than one original has been issued, all originals must be presented.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Date
isbp821.text: The date of the insurance document must be no later than the date of shipment, unless the document indicates that cover is effective from a date not later than the date of shipment.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Currency
isbp821.text: The currency of the insurance document must be the same as the currency of the credit.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — 110% Minimum
isbp821.text: The amount of insurance coverage must be at least 110% of the CIF or CIP value of the goods.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Coverage Route
isbp821.text: The insurance must cover the goods at least from the place of taking in charge or shipment to the place of discharge or final destination as stated in the credit.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Risks
isbp821.text: Where the credit uses imprecise terms such as 'usual risks', the insurance document is accepted as presented without regard to risks not covered.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — All Risks
isbp821.text: When a credit requires 'all risks' coverage, an insurance document containing any 'all risks' notation will be accepted regardless of any risks stated to be excluded.

isbp821.heading: Insurance — Goods and Voyage Description
isbp821.text: The description of the goods, voyage and shipment details on the insurance document must not conflict with data in the invoice, transport document or other stipulated documents.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Issuer
isbp821.text: A certificate of origin must be issued by the entity stated in the credit. If no issuer is stated, banks accept a certificate that appears to fulfil the function.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Beneficiary or Chamber
isbp821.text: When a credit requires the certificate of origin to be issued by the beneficiary, exporter or manufacturer, a certificate issued by a chamber of commerce that clearly identifies the beneficiary, exporter or manufacturer is also acceptable.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Country
isbp821.text: The country of origin shown on the certificate of origin must not conflict with the country of origin (if any) shown on the invoice or other stipulated documents.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Goods
isbp821.text: The description of goods on the certificate of origin may be general but must not conflict with the credit or invoice description.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Consignee
isbp821.text: Consignee information on the certificate of origin must not conflict with the consignee information on the transport document.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Signature
isbp821.text: A certificate of origin must be signed unless the credit indicates otherwise.

isbp821.heading: Certificate of Origin — Signature Requirements
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires a signed certificate of origin, it must bear what appears to be a handwritten or authenticated signature.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Content
isbp821.text: Where a credit requires a certificate or declaration, every condition or requirement stated in the credit for that certificate must be addressed in the document.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Issuer
isbp821.text: A certificate must be issued by the entity stated in the credit. If no issuer is stated, the document may be issued by any party.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Signature
isbp821.text: Where a credit requires a certificate to be signed, it must bear what appears to be a handwritten or authenticated signature. A stamp or seal alone does not constitute a signature.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Cross-references
isbp821.text: Where a certificate references another document such as the invoice or bill of lading by number or date, those references must match the corresponding documents.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Non-conflict
isbp821.text: Data in a certificate must not conflict with data in any other stipulated document or the credit.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — LC Reference
isbp821.text: Where the credit requires a certificate to quote the credit number, the absence of such reference is a discrepancy.

isbp821.heading: Certificates — Timeframe
isbp821.text: Where a certificate states a timeframe (e.g., 'within X days of shipment'), it must match the timeframe specified in the credit.
